conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have two children - Alex and Blake. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! I'm glad to help you work through this.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex and Blake, I'll need to ask you a few questions about each of them and your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How old are Alex and Blake?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Both Alex and Blake are under 16, which is a good start.

Now, could you tell me: **Are you responsible for Alex and Blake?** By this I mean, do they live with you, or do you contribute to the cost of looking after them at least the same amount as Child Benefit would provide?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex lives with me at home. Blake doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially with their costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

For Blake, since they don't live with you but you contribute financially, could you tell me a bit more:

**Who does Blake live with, and how much do you contribute towards Blake's costs each week?** 

(For reference, the current Child Benefit rate is £26.05 per week for an eldest or only child, and £17.25 per week for additional children.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Blake is in care at the moment - they've been there for about a month or so. I contribute £26.05 a week towards their upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know about Blake's situation.

I have a follow-up question about Blake: **Has the local authority contributed to Blake's accommodation or maintenance costs at any point during the time they've been in care?**

Also, just to confirm for both children: **Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

As for Blake, I'm not sure what you mean exactly. Blake is in local authority care, so the council is looking after them there, if that's what you're asking?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Yes, that's exactly what I was asking about. Since Blake is in local authority care and the council is looking after them, this is an important factor for Child Benefit eligibility.

When a child has been in local authority care (looked after by the council) for more than 8 weeks, unfortunately the person who was previously claiming Child Benefit is no longer eligible to receive it for that child. You mentioned Blake has been in care for about a month, so around 4 weeks.

**Do you expect Blake to remain in local authority care for more than 8 weeks in total, or are they likely to return home before then?**

Also, one more question: **Are both Alex and Blake British citizens, or do they have the right to live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure how long Blake will be in care - it's still being figured out by social services. As for your other question, yes, both kids are British citizens.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand the situation with Blake is uncertain at the moment.

Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex or Blake?** For example, another parent or guardian?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. For Blake, I don't think anyone else is claiming either - they're in care, so I'm the one contributing to their costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question: **Are Alex and Blake in full-time education or training?** (This is mainly relevant for children approaching 16, but I want to make sure I have the full picture for Blake who is 15.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is only 13, so they're just in regular school. Blake is 15 and was in school before going into care - I assume they're still doing some education there, but I'm not entirely sure of the details.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for all the information you've provided. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for both Alex and Blake.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, here's my assessment:

---

## Child Benefit Eligibility

### Alex ✅ Eligible
You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. They are under 16, live with you in the UK, they are a British citizen, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for them. You meet all the criteria.

### Blake ✅ Currently Eligible (with an important condition)
You are **currently** eligible to claim Child Benefit for Blake. Although Blake is in local authority care, you can continue to claim Child Benefit for up to **8 weeks** from when they entered care. Since Blake has only been in care for about 4 weeks, you're still within this period.

**However, please be aware:** If Blake remains in local authority care for **more than 8 weeks in total**, your eligibility for Child Benefit for Blake will end at that point. Given that the situation is still being figured out by social services, I'd recommend keeping track of the timeline and being prepared for your eligibility to potentially change.

---

If you have any questions or your circumstances change, please don't hesitate to seek further guidance. I hope this has been helpful!
